summary: Frequent 429s for short-lived streaming sessions created in micro-bursts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a spike of 429 responses when their fleet of small worker processes (thousands of very short-lived clients) open streaming sessions in tight micro-bursts (hundreds of concurrent starts in <1s windows). The customer uses ephemeral connections that create a new streaming handshake for each request.

Impact:
- End users see failed responses (429) on ~15-30% of starts during bursts.
- Observed increased client-side retries causing higher downstream customer cost and degraded UX.
- Affects production traffic for BrightLearn's personalization service between 09:00-11:00 UTC.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod, us-east)
- Customer tier: enterprise (BrightLearn Inc.)
- Endpoints: POST /v1/streams/chat and long-poll websocket upgrades via the streaming-proxy
- Models: redwood-vicuna-13b-q4 primary, open-llm-13b fallback

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Launch 2,000 short-lived worker processes that each: open streaming session, send a 1-2 token system prompt, close after receiving the first streamed token.
2) Coordinate bursts so that ~200-400 new connections are initiated within a 500ms window.
3) Observe 429 responses on a fraction of requests and increased 500s from pooled proxies under load.

Expected behavior:
- Small streaming sessions should be accepted and routed; short-window counters should not penalize high churn if global quotas permit the throughput.

Actual behavior:
- Per-tenant short-window counters and per-connection handshake accounting appear to increment considerably for each session start, causing the rate-limiter to issue 429s before token-level quotas are consumed.

Logs / Observations (pulled by customer & support):
- Edge logs show many REQUEST_START events clustered at 2026-03-12T09:12:03.123Z with identical tenant_id and ephemeral_key id prefixes.
- Rate-limiter decision traces: "REJECT short_window_exceeded tenant=brightlearn tenant_window=300ms used=230 allowed=200"
- Gateway metrics: connection_establish_latency median=35ms p95=120ms; connection_teardown high.
- Sample client-side error: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  X-RateLimit-Reason: tenant_short_window_exhausted

Temporary mitigations tried by customer before ticket:
- Introduced fixed 10ms sleep between starts (reduced 429s but did not eliminate).
- Switched to keep-alive/reuse of streaming sessions for some workers (reduced surface area).
- Increased client-side exponential backoff (helps but increases end-to-end latency).

Notes on why this looks different from a simple token bucket exhaustion:
- The spike pattern is characterized by many short-lived connections; each connection emits a handshake that the edge counts separately for a short-window concurrency metric (different from the long-running token budget).
- We suspect interplay between per-connection charge, short-window sliding counter, and per-tenant concurrency cap.

Request from customer:
- Explanation of why starts are being counted so aggressively and guidance for configuration changes (server-side and recommended client-side best practices) to avoid 429s without forcing them to serialise traffic dramatically.
comments: 2026-03-12 10:05 - Aisha Patel (Support): Ticket created after receiving alert from BrightLearn CS. Collected initial logs and asked for a sample client reproducer and timing of the bursts.

2026-03-12 12:40 - BrightLearn (Customer): Uploaded a lightweight reproducible script (attached in the portal) that launches 1,500 ephemeral clients that each open and close a stream after first token. Reports consistent 15-30% 429 rate during 09:00-11:00 window.

2026-03-12 13:10 - Sanjay Kapoor (SRE): Observed short-window rejects in the edge decision traces matching customer's tenant_id. Adding analysis tasks to verify whether short-window is misconfigured or correctly enforcing expected microburst window.

2026-03-13 09:22 - Marco Diaz (API): Confirmed related metrics in apigw: per-second start-count spike correlates with the customer's reported times. Suggest enabling tenant short-window smoothing as experiment.

2026-03-14 08:46 - Evelyn Huang (Platform Eng): Ran a controlled test from our internal harness using the customer's script; reproduced 429 pattern. Collected additional traces and opened PR to add sampling to decision-trace logs (see related_github_prs).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12: Initial hypothesis - short_window sliding counter threshold (default 200 starts/300ms) triggered by clustered session starts. Need to confirm config values for enterprise tenants.
2026-03-13: Confirmed edge rate-limiter treats 'stream start' as an atomic unit with weight=1. Handshake path increments the short-window counter before routing to serving runtime.
2026-03-13: Observed that ephemeral API key fanout and edge multi-host normalization can double-count starts in rare host-swap window (edge path normalization rule #42).
2026-03-14: Reproduced locally. Enabling tenant short-window smoothing (experimental) reduced 429s from 25% -> 4% in controlled run. Further validation in staging required.

Action items: (1) Validate tenant-level short-window config for BrightLearn (SRE). (2) Add smoothing toggle and run A/B test behind feature flag (Platform Eng). (3) Update docs with client best practices for microburst patterns (DevX).
resolution: Workaround recommended: (a) Customer to reuse streaming sessions where feasible and introduce small randomized jitter on session start; (b) Support to enable tenant short-window smoothing toggle for BrightLearn (temporary mitigation) and monitor for regressions. Root cause: edge short-window counter semantics + handshake accounting cause microburst starts to be rejected even when token budget exists. Permanent fix: implement smoothing and adjust host-normalization logic to avoid double-counting ephemeral-key handoffs. Work to be tracked in linked internal tickets and PRs.
